caveats: 1 repetition per cell; no significance can be claimed. Baseline variance alone spans the full score range observed.
output_tokens are completion tokens only; the raw record has no input-token field.
The judge criteria are strict about a literal 'Not needed' section, which both arms often omit, so the YAGNI case discriminates format compliance as much as principle choice.
Plan-endpoint file persistence interacts badly with the harness: it caused a cross-run /tmp leak (now cleaned per run) and voided one opus run via a write-approval prompt.
findings: Only one genuine positive: opus-4.8-medium YAGNI case, CHANGE 100.0 vs BASE 30.0 (judge: CHANGE listed the registry, YAML config, and adapter layer under Not needed; BASE deferred them without the section).
Sonnet-4.6-medium showed no separation on either case: all four runs scored 30.0.

BASELINE IS NON-DETERMINISTIC AT n=1: in an earlier clean run the sonnet baseline scored 100 on the dry case (extracted a shared validator); in this run the identical baseline scored 30. An earlier claim that the trilogy caused a regression was baseline variance, and is retracted.

Across both clean sonnet runs the CHANGE arm chose KISS on the dry case and emitted the pre-change 'KISS Breakdown' block name rather than the new 'Principle Breakdown' format, despite the updated skill being verified present in the workspace.
The DRY case never produced a pass in any arm or model, so the ordered-selection-table fix remains unproven.
Hard gates (no premature implementation, no speculative design) passed in all 8 runs.

voided_runs.reason: final_text is a 131-char write-approval prompt; the plan was produced in-session but not captured by the adapter, so the judge scored no deliverable
